title: PT2 — Community Immunity Story: A Public Health Campaign
summary: Design a mini public-health campaign that teaches your community how vaccines work and why herd immunity protects everyone.
instructions:
Your task is to create a public-health campaign that educates your barangay, family, or school about vaccines and immunity. You will:

  1. Choose ONE campaign format:
    • Poster or infographic (PDF, PNG, or hand-drawn photographed)
    • Short video PSA (1–2 minutes, mobile video is fine)
    • Comic strip or storyboard (4–8 panels)
    • Radio/audio jingle or 60-second script with recording
  2. Explain the science of how vaccines work:
    • What a vaccine contains (weakened, inactivated, or partial pathogen)
    • How the immune system responds (B cells, T cells, memory cells)
    • How memory cells make future infections harmless
  3. Focus on ONE vaccine-preventable disease in the Philippines:
    • Examples: measles (tigdas), polio, hepatitis B, diphtheria, tetanus, COVID-19
    • Why it matters locally — cases, outbreaks, or risks in your community
  4. Introduce the idea of herd immunity:
    • How many people need to be vaccinated to protect a community
    • Who is protected when herd immunity is reached (babies, elderly, immunocompromised)
  5. Address ONE common vaccine misconception with scientific evidence. Examples:
    • "Vaccines cause autism" — debunked by extensive studies
    • "Vaccines give you the disease" — explained by how vaccines train immunity safely
    • "Natural immunity is always better" — explained by the risks of the actual disease
  6. Include a call to action: What should your audience DO after seeing your campaign?
  7. Share your campaign with at least 3 people (family, classmates, or neighbors) and document it with a short note or photo.
  8. Reflect (2–3 paragraphs) on what you learned and why community awareness matters for public health.

Format: Submit as PDF, video, audio, or image. Include a copy of your script/plan and evidence of sharing.
requirements: Campaign in one of the approved formats (poster, video, comic, audio)
Explanation of how vaccines work (B cells, T cells, memory cells)
One specific vaccine-preventable disease in the Philippines
Explanation of herd immunity with numbers
Debunking of one common vaccine misconception with evidence
Clear call to action for the audience
Evidence of sharing with at least 3 people
Citations of sources used (APA or MLA)
